thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: P0 - Serving runtime: repeated GPU node flaps + NCCL communicator failures detected in prod cluster (region: us-west1). Paging on-call: @oncall-rohan :rotating_light:

oncall-rohan: Acknowledged. Pulling logs now, will update in 2.

sahil: seeing the same—multiple model-serving pods with 'NCCL ERROR 3 : unhandled cuda error' and kernel driver resets. Some tasks showing OOM before crash.

eng-runtime: tag:runtime-v3.8.1 had a canary in us-west1 that started failing ~ 11:03 UTC. We have automated fallback configured but it didn't trigger for all routes.

support-lina: Customer impact — three customers running high-throughput pipeline-parallel workloads reported errors and increased latencies. Two reported failed batch jobs. Raising CS incident for them.

oncall-rohan: quick snapshot of logs from one affected pod:

```
E NCCL WARN Overlapping communicator destroy
E NCCL ERROR 3 : unhandled cuda error
[2026-03-15T11:03:19Z] cuda: driver: lost device (CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS)
[2026-03-15T11:03:19Z] runtime: aborting, abort reason: communicator aborted
```

oncall-rohan: kubectl -n rl get pods | egrep 'runtime|model' shows several CrashLoopBackOff on gpu nodes node-gpu-03/04.

infra-ana: I'm seeing node dmesg with repeated 'NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:6b:00: GPU has fallen off the bus' on node-gpu-04. Could be driver + NVLink flakiness.

eng-runtime: also observed NCCL timeouts on the allreduce path during pipeline parallel sync, causing hangs and then CUDA resets. This looks like a multi-GPU collective instability rather than a single-model bug.

oncall-rohan: Immediate mitigation plan (short-lived):
- cordon node-gpu-04 and drain remaining runtime pods to other healthy nodes
- set model routing to prefer single-GPU variants for incoming requests for affected customers
- enable NCCL async error handling env var on runtime pods to attempt graceful teardown: NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1
- temporary autoscaler bump to absorb rerouted traffic

sahil: I can push the routing change. Which config key do we toggle?

eng-runtime: use the console rollback endpoint OR:
```
# lightweight CLI fallback (run from ops):
rwctl routing set --policy=single-gpu-fallback --scope=us-west1 --selector=model=llm-pp-highmem
```

oncall-rohan: sahil please flip that, then confirm by watching traffic split in Console. I'll cordon/drain nodes.

deploy-bot: Deploy request accepted by infra-ana: patch/nccl-async-handling -> runtime-v3.8.1+patch. RequestID: DPL-9321

infra-ana: cordoned node-gpu-04, draining 12 pods. Draining shows 10 moved successfully, 2 stuck due to local volumes — forcing eviction.

support-lina: Customer A (enterprise-corp) MX jobs saw 100% failure rate for the 11:00-11:12 window. They've been notified and routed to CS SLA.

maya: I'm running quick health checks on nvlink topology, running nvidia-smi topo --matrix on node-gpu-03/04. node-gpu-04 shows broken links to 6b:00 and 6c:00.

eng-runtime: Suggest we also toggle NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 for pods on nodes using IB for collectives, to force fallback to PCIe since IB may be exacerbating the COMM timeouts.

oncall-rohan: sahil, after rwctl change — confirm traffic is down to single-gpu variants.

sahil: rwctl responded okay. Traffic routing shift started at 11:07:22 UTC, ~85% routed to single-gpu variant within 90s. Realtime metrics show request error rate falling from 18% -> 4% by 11:10.

eng-runtime: good. Stopping new multi-GPU rollouts for the model group until we validate kernel/driver stability.

infra-ana: performed node restart on node-gpu-04's host (soft reboot) after draining. After reboot, dmesg still shows occasional PCIe Bus Reset logs but GPU didn't fall off. NV driver reports a couple of ECC errors. We're isolating memory ECC as possible root contributor.

oncall-rohan: interim status: nodes cordoned: node-gpu-04 (drained), node-gpu-03 partially drained. Traffic rerouted to single-gpu fallback. Error rates trending down. Incident severity: P1 -> will keep as P0 while still impacting throughput for some customers.

support-lina: Logged impacted customers + timestamps to raft CS doc: https://redwood.internal/cs/incidents/1782009999 (internal link).

eng-runtime: Action taken on runtime side: patched runtime pods with these env vars (applied to canaries first):
```
NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1
NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
```
Restart policy: rolling restart across nodes with 30s stagger.

oncall-rohan: after patch and routing fallback, CPU/GPU utilization normalized and no new NCCL ERROR lines in logs for ~12m. Keeping monitoring window open 30m.

maya: running quick perf regression on single-gpu variant — some latency increase expected but within SLO for affected customers.

infra-ana: we will repro in a staging cluster with the same kernel/driver combo to validate. If reproducible, we'll schedule driver upgrade on hosts (recommended to 525.89+).

eng-runtime: also adding a runtime patch to detect repeated communicator hangs and fallback to local (per-node) allreduce or non-blocking fallback path. I'll open the PR.

sahil: handoff note — I need to step off pager in 25m. Who will take next on-call?

oncall-rohan: I'll hand to infra-ana for the next 2 hours to watch node stability. ana, can you take handoff?

infra-ana: taking it. I'll continue verifying node-level telemetry and coordinate staging repro.

deploy-bot: Auto-post: canary patch runtime-v3.8.1+patch promoted at 11:16 UTC to 20% after verification.

support-lina: Customer update posted at 11:20: "We've implemented routing fallbacks and are mitigating GPU instability; latency and errors should be reduced. Engineering is investigating root cause and will follow up."

oncall-rohan: summary so far (will paste into incident ticket):
- Root symptoms: NCCL communicator timeouts causing multi-GPU allreduce hangs, then GPU driver resets and pod crashloop/ooms.
- Immediate mitigations: cordon+drain affected nodes, routing fallback to single-gpu variants, env toggles (NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1, NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1), staged runtime rolling restart.
- Status: Error rate reduced from 18% -> 3-5%; major customers routed to fallback. Nodes stable after reboot and driver checks.
- Next steps: reproduce in staging (infra), kernel/driver upgrade plan (infra), runtime fallback implementation (eng-runtime), postmortem (owner: eng-runtime).

eng-runtime: created GH issue: redwood/runtime#1462 with reproduction checklist and link to logs. Assigning to team for code changes.

infra-ana: creating maintenance window to upgrade drivers next Tuesday 02:00 UTC for affected pools.

sahil: leaving pager now — thanks all.

oncall-rohan: handing off to infra-ana at 11:29 UTC. infra-ana: please escalate back to me if we see reoccurrence. :white_check_mark:

infra-ana: acknowledged. I'll post updates in this thread.

(11:55 UTC) infra-ana: quick update — staging repro succeeded at 11:44 UTC with stress test harness (pp_sync workload). We get similar NCCL timeout pattern under sustained allreduce. Stack traces and nvml telemetry attached to GH issue.

(12:20 UTC) eng-runtime: implemented non-blocking-allreduce fallback in a hotfix branch and validated in staging. Will schedule small canary tomorrow.

(12:33 UTC) support-lina: CS follow-ups completed for impacted customers. No active escalations.

(12:40 UTC) incident-bot: Incident 1782009999 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager released from oncall-rohan to infra-ana. Postmortem owner: eng-runtime.

(12:50 UTC) eng-runtime: postmortem draft created and linked in ticket; will include timeline, mitigations, and recommended changes: add automatic fallback for multi-gpu hangs, better NVLink health telemetry, and driver upgrade cadence.

(13:00 UTC) infra-ana: closing note for now — nodes in us-west1 stable, routing remains on single-gpu fallback until we complete driver upgrade and runtime patching. Will update maintenance ticket with schedule. :lock:

-- end thread --
